contrasts.estimator: FE or RE (Hausman-selected) with Driscoll-Kraay SE
contrasts.evidence: Table 2, p. 3533, direct column for Lninter: high-income vs upper-middle-income
contrasts.notes: Dependent variable is the gender gap (male minus female LFPR), so a negative coefficient narrows the gap (benefit); direction coded on benefit = -b. contrasts.notes: Dependent variable is the gender gap (male minus female LFPR), so a negative coefficient narrows the gap (benefit); direction coded on benefit = -b. Group N only; group country counts not stated (full sample 19 G20 countries). Minus signs are absent from the txt5 extraction: b is negative only where the text states a negative effect, otherwise null. upper-middle-income sign not stated in text (magnitude 0.004 printed without sign). Moderating model (digitalization x globalization term) estimated separately by income group; coefficient is the interaction term.
